propositions: JiraDataCenterTransport wraps pycontribs/jira as an opt-in extra and returns raw payload dicts (not jira.Issue objects) matching the existing verified-fake contract
Config keys JIRA_URL, JIRA_PROJECT come from typed [tool.rebar.jira] section (fail-loud on ConfigError) while JIRA_PAT is env-only and passed as token_auth bearer token
HTTP errors are attempted exactly once; connection timeouts and socket-layer TimeoutError are retried with 2s/5s backoff matching the Cloud ACLI transport
Non-https base_url is rejected unless allow_insecure=true; certificate verification is never disabled even with allow_insecure set (which affects URL scheme only); ca_bundle configures internal CAs
resolved_statuses config key sets the DC absence-probe's resolved-status set (default {Resolved, Done, Cancelled}), defaulting because server workflow names are arbitrary

The DC backend self-registers via import in adapters/__init__.py so select_backend('jira-datacenter') resolves after importing rebar_reconciler.adapters; omitting this import breaks at runtime with BackendRegistryError, not caught by unit tests of transport alone
